episodes.215768: An isolated thunderstorm developed across southern Harvey County during the early evening hours. This thunderstorm slowly moved to the south before producing damaging winds in south Wichita.
episodes.215801: During the 26th late afternoon and evening, a moist and unstable air mass interacted with an approaching upper-level disturbance and surface cold front across central and southern Indiana. Warm surface temperatures and high dew points fueled moderate instability, allowing scattered convective cells to initiate and rapidly intensify into strong to severe thunderstorms.||The severe weather event began in Howard County around 16:33 EST, where a severe thunderstorm produced 1.00-inch diameter hail near Russiaville. As the convective activity propagated south-southeastward through the evening, storms transitioned primarily into strong wind producers. Thunderstorm wind gusts estimated between 58 mph and 65 mph (50 to 56 knots) impacted multiple counties, including Morgan, Brown, Monroe, Lawrence, Jackson, Knox, and Martin between 18:41 EST and 21:35 EST. Peak estimated wind gusts reached up to 56 knots in Jackson and Martin counties.||The primary severe impact was scattered wind damage to trees. Thunderstorm wind gusts downed numerous trees, large tree limbs, and a few power lines. In Morgan County, fallen trees blocked a roadway and struck a utility pole, initiating a localized fire. Tree damage was widespread across Jackson and Martin counties which caused temporary road blockages and localized power outages throughout the affected areas.
episodes.215808: A decaying mesoscale convective system (MCS) moved southward into Alabama from Tennessee during the daytime of August 26, associated with a shortwave moving around the eastern periphery of a ridge centered over the Southwest U.S. As activity reached Central Alabama during the afternoon, storms reignited in spots while moving southeastward, briefing becoming severe at times and producing isolated areas of wind damage. Most affected was the area of Sumter County around Cuba and York.
episodes.215810: A backdoor front moved through much of eastern New Mexico during the morning hours of August 25th as the center of a very strong upper high moved over south central New Mexico. Higher moisture and upslope surface flow behind the backdoor front resulted in thunderstorm development across the east slopes of the central mountain chain midday with thunderstorms moving east and southeast across the eastern plains during the afternoon and early evening hours. Thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts at Clayton Municipal Airport and at a ZiaMet station east of Fort Sumner before exiting into West Texas around sunset. Upslope surface flow continued across eastern New Mexico on August 26th resulting in strong to severe thunderstorm development across this part of the state. One thunderstorm brought some severe hail to Dilia in far northwest Guadalupe County. Storms coalesced into a line across east central and southeast New Mexico during the evening hours before exiting into West Texas around midnight.
episodes.215964: On the afternoon of the 25th, a weak surface boundary settled over the southern Texas Panhandle into eastern New Mexico. Upslope easterly flow on the northern side of this boundary created thunderstorms off the higher terrain of eastern New Mexico. An initial cluster of thunderstorms developed in a mesoscale convective system that propagated to the southeast across the Texas Panhandle during the late afternoon and evening hours. A very dry sub-cloud layer allowed these storms to produce severe wind gusts extending as far south as the southeastern Texas Panhandle. Additionally, a strong outflow boundary out ahead of the main thunderstorm activity produced several severe wind gusts.||High wind gusts (non-thunderstorms) from Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet sites are listed below:||62 mph at Muleshoe (Bailey County),|59 mph at Earth (Lamb County), and|58 mph at Guthrie (King County).
episodes.216193: In the afternoon of August 26, discrete thunderstorms developed and one of these storms produced 1-inch diameter hail over northern Kosciusko county.
episodes.216479: Isolated to scattered strong to severe storms moved across the CWA to the north and south of the North Platte River Valley. Several storms produced large hail with one storm producing damaging winds.
episodes.216480: Isolated to scattered strong to severe storms moved across the CWA to the north and south of the North Platte River Valley. Several storms produced large hail with one storm producing damaging winds.
episodes.216481: A couple of strong to severe storms moved across Laramie County, producing large hail just north of Cheyenne. Severe Thunderstorm Watch 629.
episodes.216560: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed into west central Arkansas during the afternoon of the 26th, as a weak cold front moved into the area. The strongest thunderstorm produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.216561: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed into southeastern Oklahoma during the late afternoon and evening of the 26th, as a weak cold front moved into the area. The strongest thunderstorm produced large hail up to golf ball size.
episodes.216860: Isolated thunderstorms, fueled by SBCAPE values near 500 J/KG and orographic lift,  developed across portions of Gila County during the mid and late afternoon hours. A thunderstorm cell developed near the Globe area, along the Pinal Creek basin and was nearly stationary for an hour resulting in over two inches of rain based on doppler radar estimates. This amount of rain in a short timespan resulted in flash flooding along the low-water crossings intersecting Pinal Creek.
episodes.216936: Strong to severe thunderstorms track east to southeast across the Denver area during the late afternoon and early evening hours of August 26th. Heavy rain and hail accompanied the stronger storms with hail up to 1.25 inch in diameter being reported.
episodes.217009: Pockets of heavy rain resulted in some localized flash flooding. In addition, a lightning strike resulted in a house fire.
episodes.217013: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.217605: On the evening of August 25, 2026, severe thunderstorms crossed from eastern Minnesota into northwestern Wisconsin, delivering dangerous cloud-to-ground lightning, localized downpours, and gusty winds. During the storm, lightning struck a campsite near Lake Superior at Herbster Beach in Bayfield County, hitting a tent occupied by a mother and her 7-year-old son and injuring them severely.
episodes.217624: A thunderstorm developed and move southward into Red Willow County in Southwest Nebraska. There were several reports of hail in the county, including one report of ping-pong ball sized hail near the intersection of US Highway 83 and Road 720.
episodes.217643: Remnant convection across western Oklahoma gradually intensified as it approached a quasi-stationary boundary during the afternoon and early evening of the 25th. Sufficient wind shear and instability produced transient supercells and organized thunderstorm clusters, leading to reports of large hail, severe wind gusts and wind damage.
episodes.217869: A weather system moved through on August 25th and brought favorable conditions for severe thunderstorms across the Texas Panhandle. A line of thunderstorms developed in the afternoon and became widespread through the evening as it moved from northwest to southeast. Damaging winds were the primary hazard, but these storms also produced some hail and caused flash flooding in some areas.
episodes.217870: A weather system moved through on August 25th and brought favorable conditions for severe thunderstorms across the western Oklahoma Panhandle. A line of thunderstorms developed in the afternoon and became widespread through the evening, but Oklahoma only suffered from northern portions of the line. Damaging winds were the primary hazard.
episodes.217892: An outflow boundary from morning convection refired over northeast Mississippi as it intersected a very warm, moist, and unstable airmass. A cluster of storms resulted in a couple of damaging wind reports.
episodes.217940: A frontal boundary dropped southward into southern GA on the 24th before stalling into the 25th. This, combined with some weak upper level energy and influences from southwest flow and the Atlantic sea breeze, resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms and isolated strong to severe cells across northeast FL. Impacts were mainly due to heavy rainfall from slow moving storms, though isolated thunderstorm wind damage also occurred.
episodes.217959: Isolated thunderstorms developed along a weak cold front and produced a few instances of hail, localized wind damage, and power outages across parts of the DFW Metroplex the evening of August 26.
episodes.218227: A heat wave developed across the region during late August. A weak boundary and short wave approached from the north causing strong to severe storms.
episodes.218459: Received a couple reports of severe wind gusts.
